3. The prayer for bail of the petitioner has been rejected vide order  dated 12.09.2023 passed by the learned Additional District & Sessions  Judge, Balliguda in BLAPL No. 80 of 2023.
4. The prosecution allegation in brief against the petitioner is that the  victim had gone with her "would be" husband to Bisam Cuttack Hospital  for her check as she had a infection in her face.

When her "would be"
 husband had gone to meet his mother, the present petitioner arrived at the  spot and gestured to the informant to show her some photographs on his  // 2 //

When she went towards him he said that he would show the photographs to her "would be" husband.

When she followed him to look at the photographs, he made her sit in the car (as per the statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.) and forced her to sit in the car (as per the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.) and said that he would not allow her to marry anybody else and took her to Rayagada.
On the way he demanded Rs.5,000/- to release her.
She gave him Rs.4,000/- out of which Rs.2,000/- had been given by her "would be" husband.
After reaching Rayagada they went to an ATM from where she withdrew Rs.1,000/-.
Using the ATM card of her "would be "husband.
When the petitioner saw that the account had a lot of money, he asked the victim to withdraw more money.
She refused and broke the ATM card and threw it.
He pulled her and made her sit in the car and they proceeded to the Railway Station.
There, he slapped her for which she fainted.
When she regained consciousness she found that they were in a train.
He told that they were going to Banglore.
At Banglore they went to his friend's house where the present petitioner removed the SIM of her mobile phone and gave the mobile to his friend.
They stayed there in a lodge for 5 days (as per the statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.) and one week (as per the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.).
During their stay, the petitioner had physical relationship with the victim without her consent as per the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.

He threatened her of dire consequences and to kill her brothers and sisters-in-law if she got married.
During their stay in the lodge, he kept physical relationship with her forcibly.
After 7 days, they returned back to Baliguda.
On the way, she borrowed the mobile phone of a girl in the ladies rest room and informed her brother (as per statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C).
Her brother and others were waiting for them at Muniguda Railway Station.
But when the petitioner saw them, he did not allow the victim to get down from the train and ultimately they get down from the train at Amadullah Station.
From there, they went to M. Rampur and then to Balliguda in a bus.

Rampur when the petitioner had gone to withdraw money from the ATM,
the victim called her brother from a mobile of a person who was there.
She was rescued by her brother.
FIR has been lodged after 8 days.

5. Dr. S. Ranjit, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the victim and the petitioner were both major and known to each other since childhood and were in love with each other since long.
As the brother of the victim was not agreeable to their marriage, he fixed her marriage with another person.
So they had eloped from the village and when they were returning to their village together, her brother took her away forcibly and tutored her to speak against him.
Therefore there is an unexplained delay of 8 days in lodging the FIR.

He also submits that there are major discrepancies in the statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, which are as follows:
(i) In the statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. she has stated that the physical relations between them were consensual and in the statement recorded under Sections 164 Cr.P.C., it has been stated that it was without her consent.
(ii) In the F.I.R. lodged by mother of the victim it is stated that 4 people kidnapped the victim threatening her "would be" husband with knife but in her statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. the victim has stated that the petitioner has taken her in the car.

(iii) In her statement recorded under Sections 164 Cr.P.C., the victim has not stated whose phone she used in ladies rest room to talk to her brother but in her statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C., she has stated that she used the phone of a girl.

He further submits that as petitioner is in custody since 14.07.2023 and chargesheet has been submitted in the meanwhile, no useful purpose would be served by detaining the petitioner in custody and he should be released on bail.
Finally, he submits that the petitioner is a victim of Indian social prejudices which is biased against the males.
As the petitioner is a man, everybody presumes that he must at fault.

4 6. Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Additional Government Advocate opposes the prayer for bail and submits that from a reading of the statements recorded under Section - 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C. of the victim,
an offence under Section 376 (2)(n) of IPC is made out against the petitioner.
He further submits that in the F.I.R. lodged by the mother of the victim it has been mentioned that the petitioner had once abducted the petitioner 6 months ago from her home at midnight.
From the prior conduct of the petitioner, it is apparent that if the petitioner is released on bail, he will try to influence the victim and tamper with prosecution evidence.

7. After the submission of Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Additional Government Advocate, Dr. S. Ranjit, learned counsel for the petitioner against submitted that any stringent conditions may be imposed by the Court for releasing the petitioner on bail so that he is not able to tamper with the evidence and that since the relationship between the petitioner and the victim was consensual, an offence under Section 376 (2) (n) of IPC is not made out.
8.

Considering the submission of the learned counsels, the ingredients of Section 376 (2) (n) of IPC, and the statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. , I am of the opinion that a prima case under Section 376 (2) of IPC is made out against the against the petitioner.

The discrepancies in the statements of the victim are not major so the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the victim should not believed as she has been tutored to give those statements is not  Page 5 of 6  // 6 //
